title: The test set cannot be passed by a lookup: unseen requests, real ones, and the user's own reactions
goal: Ask scored 92 of 100 on drawings while the user found it drew one cat for every cat request. The test set has to measure what a person feels: requests the climbing runner never sees, requests taken from what people really type (poses, scenes, styles, edits), and the user's own thumbs on Ask's rows feeding back in as cases.
notes: The user, 2026-10-20: 'i really don't think this model is great. i'm wondering what the process looks like on making it better?' Score history (queue/evals/ask-eval-history.jsonl): Ask on qwen3:30b 37.8 vs the skill on a frontier model 83.9 on the same tools (drawing 35 vs 87, sheet 47 vs 74, layout 30 vs 82); the dog task then climbed Ask's drawings to 92 mostly with a built-in Twemoji set looked up by noun, which is exactly what the user then found wrong. Classic overfitting to a small visible set. Runs before the model bake-off so the bake-off is measured on the honest set.
acceptance: A held-out set of at least 40 requests lives apart from the cases a runner climbs on, and a runner working on Ask reports both scores but may only read the held-out cases' results in total, never one by one, so a fix cannot be shaped to them. It includes poses, scenes, styles, edits of an existing drawing, and the user's own failures to date

The rubric's didWhatWasAsked is judged against every word of the request: a stock drawing that ignores 'curled up sleeping' scores 2 or lower however clean it is. The user's cat pictures (queue/audits/2026-10-20-user-ask-cat-sleeping-same-cat.png, queue/audits/2026-10-20-user-ask-cat-playing-piano.png) score low on today's build
Each Ask change row gets a quiet thumbs up and down; a thumbs down saves the request, the document before and the result as a new held-out case, so the set grows from real use
The eval reports, per run, how often the result came from a stored drawing or a coded template versus drawn for the request, so climbing by lookup shows up as a number

Today's build scored on the new set in the audit as the honest baseline. Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not

log.note: intake 2026-10-20: the user ruled out hardcoded anything. Count code that draws a named subject (IllustrationPieces.swift: fox, lighthouse, skyline, mountains...) in the stored-or-coded share, not only the stored Twemoji set, and pick held-out subjects none of that code covers.

Adversarial review before building: (1) a held-out set a runner can read is not held out, so the eval itself must refuse to print held-out cases, and the runner contract must forbid opening them; (2) a stricter rubric line alone does not fix the score: a clean stock cat that ignores 'sleeping' still scored about 85 because rules, three other judge lines and a blind look saying 'cat' carry it, so the score must be gated on didWhatWasAsked; (3) the user's own failures were already filed as climb cases on the scene task, which would leak them out of the held-out set; (4) thumbs that only show on hover cannot be proven by a background walk and are harder to find.

Reproduced the user's report on today's build first: the walk asked 'draw a cat curled up sleeping' and got the standing built-in cat, named 'Sleeping Cat', source 'stored' (ask-row-thumbs-walk, /tmp/photonz-playtest/ask-row-thumbs-walk/1-row-sc.png).

Built: PhotonzCore AskFeedback.swift (AskDrawingSource read from each add_drawing answer's from; AskVerdict; AskFeedbackCase + folderName), AskChangeList rows carry sources and a verdict with vote() (tests: AskFeedbackTests, 8). App: AskSession records lastSources/lastModel and vote(_:on:in:) writes case.json, before.photonz, after.photonz, after.png to ~/Library/Application Support/<bundle>/Ask feedback/<time-request>/; the walk state shows ask.sources; AskViews puts thumbs up/down in each row and Good Result / Bad Result in its right-click menu.

Chose always-visible faint thumbs (secondary at 70%, filled and primary when picked) over hover-revealed ones because the hover version could not be pressed by a walk running behind other apps (first walk run failed: 'reads not picked') and a person has to find them to use them.

Eval: Scripts/ask-eval/held-out/ holds 42 cases (user's 2 cat failures, 7 poses, 8 scenes, 9 styles, 8 edits of drawings Ask made, saved as held-out/starts/*.photonz by thumbs votes, 2 icons, 3 layouts, 3 redlines). run --set held-out prints only totals, refuses --cases, draws no sheet, records no per-case scores; report prints climb and held-out side by side; feedback imports thumbs down (not the probe's) as use-*.json cases started from the saved before.photonz; lookups.mjs tallies stored/template/drawn for both engines (tests lookups.test.mjs, 6). Rubric didWhatWasAsked judged on every word, and scoring.mjs scales a case by didWhatWasAsked/7 when under 7.

Calibration on the new rubric (ebbf2873) agrees with the user on all 7 pictures: the user's sleeping cat didWhatWasAsked 1 (case at best 10), the piano cat didWhatWasAsked 1 (case at best 9.7), the clean sheet still 8.

Moved the user's two cat requests out of a-scene-of-things-doing-something-together-is-dr's climb list (now a rabbit curled up asleep, a cat playing a guitar) and logged why there. ask-draws-any-subject-well-with-nothing-stored-o (filed by the user while this ran) asks for held-out contact sheets in its audit: allowed once, after the last change, in runner-prompt and README.

Ask rows carry a faint thumbs up/down (and Good/Bad Result in the right-click menu); a vote saves request + before/after documents + picture under Application Support/<bundle>/Ask feedback, and Scripts/ask-eval.sh feedback turns thumbs down into held-out cases (ask-row-thumbs-walk, pointer press at Next defaults, case.json verified). Scripts/ask-eval/held-out: 42 unseen cases incl. the user's two cat failures, poses, scenes, styles, 8 edits of saved drawings, icons, layouts, redlines; --set held-out prints/records totals only; report shows climb and held-out side by side; runner-prompt forbids reading held-out cases. Lookups counted per run (stored/template/drawn) for both engines. Rubric judges every word; cases under 7 on didWhatWasAsked are scaled down; calibration agrees on all 7 user pictures (both cats didWhatWasAsked 1, case at best ~10). Baseline rubric ebbf2873: held-out 20.1 (85% of drawings looked up), climb 78.2 (100%). Tests: Scripts/test.sh 14094 passed; node --test lookups.test.mjs 6, rules.test.mjs 14. Audit queue/audits/2026-10-20-the-test-set-cannot-be-passed-by-a-lookup-unseen.json. Follow-up: find-out-why-ask-sometimes-waits-five-minutes-fo (p2).
